top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks to Katori and Ye is the most mature and cleanly allocated option: magic-wavelength trapping is a single physical idea, and its 1e-18 realisation has been reproduced and cross-compared at JILA/NIST, RIKEN/Tokyo, SYRTE and PTB, with new physics already extracted (millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, bounds on varying constants and ultralight dark matter). The citation must stay on the lattice clock, not the comb or the redefinition of the second, to avoid re-crediting 2005. Twisted bilayer graphene is second as a genuine prediction-then-discovery but still young with unresolved pairing and an unavoidable credit gap (Cao and others); IceCube is third because the diffuse flux is secure but the Halzen/Spiering allocation is unsettled; no award is last since a robust, reproducible discovery is available.
recusal_note: Possible but weak: as WACQT director and a Chalmers superconducting-circuits theorist I have no direct tie to atomic clocks, twisted graphene or IceCube; none apparent that would bear on this slate.
